# `mortgage-data`

Unified mortgage data management CLI

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--install-completion`: Install completion for the current shell.
* `--show-completion`: Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `version`: Show version information.
* `info`: Show project information and status.
* `hmda`: HMDA data operations

* `fnma`: Fannie Mae data operations
* `fhlmc`: Freddie Mac data operations
* `umbs`: UMBS data operations
* `match`: Matching workflows for linking records
* `usps-crosswalk`: USPS ZIP crosswalk data operations

* `combined`: Combined cross-source master datasets

* `raw`: Raw download ledger: register, audit,...

## `mortgage-data hmda`

HMDA data operations

**Usage**:


**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `download`: Download HMDA data files from the CFPB...
* `bronze`: Build the bronze (raw → parquet) layer for...
* `silver`: Build the silver (Hive-partitioned) layer...
* `pipeline`: Build bronze and silver in one step (the...
* `info`: Display HMDA configuration information.

### `mortgage-data hmda download`

Download HMDA data files from the CFPB file servers.

Files land in subdirectories of the raw layer by record type:
`loans/`, `panel/`, `transmittal_series/`,
`msamd/`, and `misc/`.

Years CFPB has not published yet are detected and reported, not treated as
failures — so the leading edge is picked up automatically once released.

Examples:
  mortgage-data hmda download
  mortgage-data hmda download --dry-run
  mortgage-data hmda download -p snapshot -t loans -t transmittal_series
  mortgage-data hmda download -p historic
  mortgage-data hmda download -p mlar --min-year 2024
  mortgage-data hmda download --refresh

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data hmda download [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-p, --products <str>`: Products to fetch: snapshot, one_year, three_year, historic, mlar (repeatable; default snapshot, one_year, three_year, historic)
* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Record types to fetch: loans, panel, transmittal_series, msamd (repeatable; default all)
* `--min-year <int>`: First filing year (default: each series&#x27; own start)
* `--max-year <int>`: Last filing year, inclusive (default: current year)
* `-o, --output-dir PATH`: Output directory for downloaded files. Defaults to subpackage raw directory.
* `--file-format <str>`: Delimiter variant to fetch: csv or pipe  [default: csv]
* `--dry-run`: Show what would be fetched without downloading
* `--refresh`: Re-download files whose size differs from the server&#x27;s (catches restatements)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `--pause SECONDS`: Seconds to pause between downloads. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data hmda bronze`

Build the bronze (raw → parquet) layer for an HMDA period.

Examples:
  mortgage-data hmda bronze post2018 --min-year 2018 --max-year 2025
  mortgage-data hmda bronze 2007-2017 --overwrite
  mortgage-data hmda bronze pre2007 --datasets loans

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data hmda bronze [OPTIONS] {period}
```

**Arguments**:

* `period`: Time period: post2018, 2007-2017, pre2007  [required]

**Options**:

* `--min-year <int>`: Minimum year to process
* `--max-year <int>`: Maximum year to process
* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets: loans, panel, transmittal_series (post2018/pre2007 only; can repeat)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data hmda silver`

Build the silver (Hive-partitioned) layer for an HMDA period.

Examples:
  mortgage-data hmda silver post2018 --min-year 2018 --max-year 2025
  mortgage-data hmda silver 2007-2017 --overwrite
  mortgage-data hmda silver pre2007 --datasets loans

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data hmda silver [OPTIONS] {period}
```

**Arguments**:

* `period`: Time period: post2018, 2007-2017, pre2007  [required]

**Options**:

* `--min-year <int>`: Minimum year to process
* `--max-year <int>`: Maximum year to process
* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets: loans, panel, transmittal_series (post2018/pre2007 only; can repeat)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data hmda pipeline`

Build bronze and silver in one step (the former ``hmda import``).

Each period&#x27;s bronze step runs first; silver runs only for datasets
whose bronze build succeeded.

Examples:
  mortgage-data hmda pipeline post2018 --min-year 2018 --max-year 2025
  mortgage-data hmda pipeline 2007-2017 --min-year 2007 --max-year 2017
  mortgage-data hmda pipeline pre2007 --min-year 1990 --max-year 2006

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data hmda pipeline [OPTIONS] {period}
```

**Arguments**:

* `period`: Time period: post2018, 2007-2017, pre2007  [required]

**Options**:

* `--min-year <int>`: Minimum year to process
* `--max-year <int>`: Maximum year to process
* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets: loans, panel, transmittal_series (post2018/pre2007 only; can repeat)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `mortgage-data gnma`

GNMA (Ginnie Mae) data operations

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data gnma [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `-V, --version`: Show version and exit
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `download`: Download GNMA data files, schema PDFs, or...
* `pipeline`: Run the end-to-end GNMA pipeline.
* `bronze`: Stage GNMA raw data files to bronze parquet.
* `silver`: Transform GNMA bronze parquet to silver...
* `info`: Display GNMA configuration information.

### `mortgage-data gnma download`

Download GNMA data files, schema PDFs, or bulk-page files.

Datasets (default `data` + `schemas`):
  - `data`: data files from the disclosure history page
  - `schemas`: schema definition PDFs. Two sources exist — the
    per-prefix disclosure-history page (`--source disclosure`,
    the default) and the master bulk-layout page (`--source layout`),
    which documents prefixes the disclosure page omits (platcoll,
    hnissuesPS/S, issrcutoff, SRF, FRR, ...)
  - `bulk`: the bulk page (bulk.ginniemae.gov), which publishes
    the latest files before they reach the history page. Opt-in, so it is
    NOT part of the default set. Undated monthly files (e.g. dailyllmni.zip)
    are renamed with their reporting period; daily snapshots are skipped
    unless `--include-daily`. Bulk downloads are tracked so a later
    history-page download overwrites them with the canonical version.

Requires valid credentials (GNMA_EMAIL and GNMA_ANSWER). Files already on
disk are skipped; pass `--overwrite` to re-download.

**Examples:**

  # Data + schemas for one prefix
  $ mortgage-data gnma download monthly

  # Data only, from 2025 onward
  $ mortgage-data gnma download llmon1 llmon2 -t data --min-date 202501

  # Pull layouts the disclosure page lacks
  $ mortgage-data gnma download platcoll SRF FRR -t schemas --source layout

  # Fetch this month&#x27;s files early from the bulk page
  $ mortgage-data gnma download -t bulk

**Common prefixes:** monthly, llmon1, llmon2, hllmon1, hllmon2

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data gnma download [OPTIONS] [prefixes]...
```

**Arguments**:

* `prefixes...`: Prefixes to download (leave empty for all)

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: What to fetch: data, schemas, bulk (repeatable; default data, schemas)
* `--source <str>`: Schema source: &#x27;disclosure&#x27; (per-prefix history page), &#x27;layout&#x27; (master bulk-layout page), or &#x27;both&#x27;.  [default: disclosure]
* `--min-date <str>`: Start date in YYYYMM format (e.g. 202501)
* `--max-date <str>`: End date in YYYYMM format (e.g. 202612)
* `--include-daily`: Bulk only: include daily snapshot files
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data gnma pipeline`

Run the end-to-end GNMA pipeline.

Executes, in order:
  1. Download data and schemas
  2. Process (stage to parquet, then transform with schemas)
  3. Analyze performance data (where applicable)

Each step can be skipped. For the download+process path without analysis,
pass `--skip-analysis`.

**Examples:**

  # Complete pipeline for one prefix
  $ mortgage-data gnma pipeline monthly

  # With a date range for analysis
  $ mortgage-data gnma pipeline llmon1 llmon2 --start-date 202301 --end-date 202312

  # Data only (download + process, no analysis)
  $ mortgage-data gnma pipeline monthly --skip-analysis

  # Process only (data already downloaded)
  $ mortgage-data gnma pipeline monthly --skip-download --skip-analysis

**Common prefixes:** monthly, llmon1, llmon2, hllmon1, hllmon2

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data gnma pipeline [OPTIONS] {prefixes}...
```

**Arguments**:

* `prefixes...`: Prefixes to process  [required]

**Options**:

* `-s, --start-date <str>`: Start date for analysis (YYYYMM)
* `-e, --end-date <str>`: End date for analysis (YYYYMM)
* `--skip-download`: Skip download step
* `--skip-processing`: Skip processing step (staging + transform)
* `--skip-analysis`: Skip analysis step
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data gnma bronze`

Stage GNMA raw data files to bronze parquet.

Converts raw text/zip files to parquet format with text content preserved
in a single column. This is the first step before schema-based silver
transformation.

**Examples:**

  # Bronze for monthly prefix
  $ mortgage-data gnma bronze monthly

  # Bronze for multiple prefixes
  $ mortgage-data gnma bronze llmon1 llmon2

**Common prefixes:** monthly, llmon1, llmon2, hllmon1, hllmon2

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data gnma bronze [OPTIONS] {prefixes}...
```

**Arguments**:

* `prefixes...`: Prefixes to stage to bronze  [required]

**Options**:

* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data gnma silver`

Transform GNMA bronze parquet to silver using schemas.

Applies schema-based parsing to staged bronze parquet files, converting
text content into structured data with proper column names and dtypes.

Existing silver files are skipped; `--overwrite` rebuilds them. The
rebuild is scoped to the `{prefix}/{record_type}` files it writes —
no other silver output is touched.

**Examples:**

  # Silver for monthly prefix (all record types)
  $ mortgage-data gnma silver monthly

  # Silver with specific record types
  $ mortgage-data gnma silver llmon1 -r L P

  # Rebuild one prefix after a schema change
  $ mortgage-data gnma silver platcoll --overwrite

  # Silver for multiple prefixes
  $ mortgage-data gnma silver llmon1 llmon2

**Valid record types:** H (Header), L (Loan), P (Pool), I (Issuer), T (Trailer)

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data gnma silver [OPTIONS] {prefixes}...
```

**Arguments**:

* `prefixes...`: Prefixes to transform to silver  [required]

**Options**:

* `-r, --record-types <str>`: Record types to process (H, L, P, I, T)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `mortgage-data fhfa`

FHFA data operations

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhfa [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

**Commands**:

* `download`: Download FHFA data files and dictionaries.
* `bronze`: Load FHFA data files (fixed-width through...
* `silver`: Transform bronze data to silver layer.
* `pipeline`: Run the FHFA pipeline (schemas -&gt; bronze...

### `mortgage-data fhfa download`

Download FHFA data files and dictionaries.

Datasets (default both, `--era current`):
  - `data`: the FHFA Public Use Database files
  - `dictionaries`: the accompanying data dictionaries

`--era hud` instead fetches the pre-FHFA GSE Public Use Database
multifamily archive (1993-2007) from HUD USER into `raw/hud_era`.
Archive zips spanning several years are fetched whole when any covered year
is in range, so `--min-year`/`--max-year` select archives,
not rows.

**Examples:**

  $ mortgage-data fhfa download
  $ mortgage-data fhfa download -t data -o /custom/path
  $ mortgage-data fhfa download --era hud
  $ mortgage-data fhfa download --era hud --min-year 1996 --max-year 1998

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhfa download [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: What to fetch: data, dictionaries (repeatable; default both). Ignored when --era hud.
* `--era <str>`: Source era: &#x27;current&#x27; (FHFA PUDB) or &#x27;hud&#x27; (pre-FHFA GSE PUDB archive, 1993-2007)  [default: current]
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Output directory (single dataset only)
* `--min-year <int>`: First HUD-era year to fetch (--era hud only)  [default: 1993]
* `--max-year <int>`: Last HUD-era year to fetch (--era hud only)  [default: 2007]
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `--pause SECONDS`: Seconds to pause between downloads. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `--timeout SECONDS`: Request timeout in seconds. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `--retries COUNT`: Number of retry attempts for failed downloads. Default: 3
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhfa bronze`

Load FHFA data files (fixed-width through 2024, CSV from 2025) to bronze layer.

Reads raw data from zip files, parses using the data dictionaries,
and saves as Parquet files in the bronze layer.

**Examples:**

  # Load SF Census Tract for 2023-2024
  $ fhfa bronze -t sf_c --min-year 2023 --max-year 2024

  # Load multiple datasets
  $ fhfa bronze -t sf_c sf_d mf_c --min-year 2023 --max-year 2023

  # Custom directories
  $ fhfa bronze -t sf_c --min-year 2023 --max-year 2023 --raw-dir /data/raw -o /data/bronze

**Valid datasets:** sf_a, sf_b, sf_c, sf_d, mf_property_b, mf_unit_b, mf_c

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhfa bronze [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets to load (e.g., sf_c sf_a)  [required]
* `--min-year <int>`: First year to load (e.g., 2023)  [required]
* `--max-year <int>`: Last year to load, inclusive (e.g., 2024)  [required]
* `--raw-dir <path>`: Raw data directory (default: data/fhfa/raw)
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Bronze output directory (default: data/fhfa/bronze)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhfa silver`

Transform bronze data to silver layer.

Applies standardization:
- Renames columns using translation dictionary
- Drops unwanted columns based on patterns
- Adds census year metadata
- Standardizes data types

**Examples:**

  # Transform SF Census Tract for 2023-2024
  $ fhfa silver -t sf_c --min-year 2023 --max-year 2024

  # Transform multiple datasets
  $ fhfa silver -t sf_c sf_d --min-year 2023 --max-year 2023

  # Custom drop patterns
  $ fhfa silver -t sf_c --min-year 2024 --max-year 2024 --drop-pattern &quot;Rural&quot; --drop-pattern &quot;Poverty&quot;

**Valid datasets:** sf_a, sf_b, sf_c, sf_d, mf_property_b, mf_unit_b, mf_c

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhfa silver [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets to transform (e.g., sf_c sf_a)  [required]
* `--min-year <int>`: First year to transform (e.g., 2023)  [required]
* `--max-year <int>`: Last year to transform, inclusive (e.g., 2024)  [required]
* `--bronze-dir <path>`: Bronze input directory (default: data/fhfa/bronze)
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Silver output directory (default: data/fhfa/silver)
* `--drop-pattern <str>`: Column patterns to drop (can specify multiple)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing silver files
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhfa pipeline`

Run the FHFA pipeline (schemas -&gt; bronze -&gt; silver).

Each step can be skipped, which covers the four previous sub-commands:
  - schemas + data (the default)   -&gt; was `pipeline full`
  - `--skip-schemas`                  -&gt; was `pipeline data-only`
  - `--skip-bronze --skip-silver`     -&gt; was `pipeline schemas-only`
  - `--era hud`                       -&gt; was `pipeline hud-era`

Data years (`--min-year`/`--max-year`) and schema-master
years (`--schema-min-year`/`--schema-max-year`) are separate
axes, since the masters span more years than any single data build.

`--era hud` runs the pre-FHFA GSE PUDB multifamily backfill
(download -&gt; bronze -&gt; silver over the 1993-2007 archive); it uses the
HUD-era year bounds and ignores the schema options.

**Examples:**

  $ mortgage-data fhfa pipeline --min-year 2018 --max-year 2023
  $ mortgage-data fhfa pipeline --skip-schemas -t sf_c
  $ mortgage-data fhfa pipeline --skip-bronze --skip-silver
  $ mortgage-data fhfa pipeline --era hud

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhfa pipeline [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets to process (default all)
* `--min-year <int>`: First data year to process  [default: 2025]
* `--max-year <int>`: Last data year, inclusive  [default: 2025]
* `--schema-min-year <int>`: First year for the schema masters  [default: 2008]
* `--schema-max-year <int>`: Last year for the schema masters  [default: 2024]
* `--era <str>`: Source era: &#x27;current&#x27; (FHFA PUDB) or &#x27;hud&#x27; (1993-2007 archive)  [default: current]
* `--skip-schemas`: Skip the schema build step
* `--skip-download`: Skip download (--era hud only)
* `--skip-bronze`: Skip bronze loading
* `--skip-silver`: Skip silver transformation
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data fhfa schemas extract`

Extract PDFs from enterprise PUDB zip files.

Convert PDFs/Excel to CSV/Parquet format.

Converts dictionary PDFs (years before 2024) and the Excel
dictionaries (2024 on) to CSV format for easier processing.

Combines year-specific dictionaries into master files that span
multiple years. Master dictionaries are saved as:
dictionary_files/fhfa/masters/master_{dataset}.csv

Run complete schema processing pipeline.

This is equivalent to running:

## `mortgage-data fnma`

Fannie Mae data operations

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fnma [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `-V, --version`: Show version and exit
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `bronze`: Import raw FNMA loan-performance zip files...
* `silver`: Build the FNMA silver layer from bronze...
* `pipeline`: Run bronze + silver for FNMA...
* `info`: Display FNMA configuration information.
* `download`: Instructions for downloading Fannie Mae...

### `mortgage-data fnma bronze`

Import raw FNMA loan-performance zip files to bronze parquet.

Datasets (default: sf, exclusions, harp, multifamily):
  - `sf`: per-quarter SF zips (YYYYQ[1-4]*.zip) in the raw
    directory -&gt; one parquet per quarter in the bronze root. Bulk archives
    are not read here; use performance_all for the Performance_All archive.
  - `exclusions`: Exclusions.zip -&gt; {YYYYQn}EXCL.parquet beside
    the standard quarters: the loans Fannie leaves out of the standard
    dataset (ARM, Alt-A, government-insured, bulk acquisitions),
    2000Q1-2020Q3. Every quarter; skipped only when the zip is absent.
  - `performance_all`: Performance_All.zip -&gt; one parquet per
    quarter, the only source of the pre-2016 history (2000Q1 forward).
    OPT-IN: not in the default set, since it restates every quarter.
    Scope it with --min-year/--max-year or --quarters; existing quarters
    are skipped unless --overwrite.
  - `harp`: HARP_Files.zip -&gt; bronze/harp/loan_performance.parquet
    (the whole HARP population in one un-partitioned panel, same 113-field
    layout as the quarterly files) + loan_mapping.parquet (the 1:1 pre-HARP
    loan bridge). Skipped when the zip is absent.
  - `multifamily`: Multifamily.zip / Multifamily_DSCR.zip -&gt;
    release-stamped parquet under bronze/multifamily/ (skipped silently
    when the zips are absent).

Examples:
  mortgage-data fnma bronze
  mortgage-data fnma bronze -t harp
  mortgage-data fnma bronze -t multifamily --overwrite
  mortgage-data fnma bronze -t performance_all -m 2000 -M 2015
  mortgage-data fnma bronze -t performance_all --quarters 2005Q3

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fnma bronze [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets to import: sf, exclusions, performance_all, harp, multifamily (repeatable; default sf, exclusions, harp, multifamily)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-m, --min-year <int>`: Lowest year to import (performance_all only).
* `-M, --max-year <int>`: Highest year to import (performance_all only).
* `--quarters <str>`: Explicit quarter stems, e.g. 2005Q3 (repeatable; performance_all only). Overrides --min-year/--max-year.
* `--tmp-dir <path>`: Extraction scratch space (performance_all, exclusions). Defaults to the data volume; the system temp dir cannot hold the back-history members (2003Q3 is 40.5 GB).
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fnma silver`

Build the FNMA silver layer from bronze loan-performance parquet.

Builds four datasets (default all):
  - `issuances`: first observation per loan (one row per loan)
  - `performance`: the full monthly panel (loan x month) with the
    ``MMYYYY`` date columns parsed to dates — the GSE SF-credit input to the
    combined `loan_performance` master
  - `harp`: the HARP performance/issuances/terminations tables plus
    the pre-HARP loan bridge, in silver/harp/. Schema-identical to the
    quarterly silver, but a DISJOINT loan population — union it in explicitly
    if a consumer wants HARP refis included
  - `multifamily`: the MF performance/acquisitions/terminations/
    current_dscr datasets from the latest bronze/multifamily/ release
    (skipped with a warning when no MF bronze exists)

Already-built outputs are skipped unless `--overwrite`. A new
multifamily release restates the full history, so rebuild it with
`-t multifamily --overwrite`.

Examples:
  mortgage-data fnma silver
  mortgage-data fnma silver -t performance
  mortgage-data fnma silver -t multifamily --overwrite

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fnma silver [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Silver datasets to build: issuances, performance, harp, multifamily (repeatable; default all)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fnma pipeline`

Run bronze + silver for FNMA loan-performance data in one step.

Download is manual (see ``fnma download``); pipeline assumes raw files are
already in place. Runs every bronze dataset, then every silver dataset —
the same sets ``fnma bronze`` / ``fnma silver`` build by default. Silver
still runs even if bronze reports failures, since previously-built bronze
parquet may still cover the requested quarters.

Examples:
  mortgage-data fnma pipeline
  mortgage-data fnma pipeline --overwrite

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fnma pipeline [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fnma info`

Display FNMA configuration information.

Shows the current configuration paths and settings for FNMA data.

Examples:
  mortgage-data fnma info
  fnma info

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fnma info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fnma download`

Instructions for downloading Fannie Mae Single-Family Loan Performance Data.

Manual Download Required

Fannie Mae data requires free registration on the Data Dynamics platform.
Automated download is not supported due to Terms of Service restrictions.

**Steps to Download:**

1. Visit the Fannie Mae data portal:
   https://capitalmarkets.fanniemae.com/credit-risk-transfer/single-family-credit-risk-transfer/fannie-mae-single-family-loan-performance-data

2. Click &quot;Access the Data&quot; to reach Data Dynamics

3. Register for a free account (email + password)

4. Accept Terms and Conditions

5. Download files to: data/fnma/raw/

**After Download:**

Run the import command to process files:
  $ mortgage-data fnma bronze

**Documentation:**

See docs/manual_downloads.md for detailed instructions.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fnma download [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhlmc silver`

Build the FHLMC silver layer from bronze parquet.

Datasets (default all):
  - `origination`: one row per Loan Sequence Number, hive-partitioned
    by vintage_year. Accepts `--min-year`/`--max-year`.
  - `performance`: the loan x month panel, one parquet per quarter
  - `crt`: the at-issuance CRT reference-pool disclosure

`reperforming` has no silver builder and is ignored if passed.

**Examples:**

  $ mortgage-data fhlmc silver
  $ mortgage-data fhlmc silver -t origination --min-year 2020
  $ mortgage-data fhlmc silver -t crt --overwrite

* `--min-year <int>`: First origination vintage (origination only)

HMDA-FHA matching workflow for linking FHA loans to HMDA applications

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-fha [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `info`: Show HMDA-FHA matching configuration and...
* `run`: Run the HMDA-FHA matching pipeline for one...
* `build-zip-tract`: Build consolidated ZIP-tract crosswalk...
* `validate`: Run validation analysis and generate...

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-fha info`

Show HMDA-FHA matching configuration and data availability, both eras.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-fha info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-fha run`

Run the HMDA-FHA matching pipeline for one era.

`--era post2018` (default):
1. Prepare FHA data
2. Prepare HMDA data (with ZIP-tract crosswalk)
3. Run the rounds in rounds.py (`info` prints them), each on the earlier rounds&#x27;
   leftovers, and write one crosswalk tagged with match_round

`--era pre2018` (2010-2017):
1. Prepare the FHA endorsement pool
2. Prepare the ZIP-fanned HMDA origination pool
3. Run the rounds in rounds.py (`info` prints them), each on the earlier rounds&#x27;
   leftovers: base key (ZIP + amount@$1k + purpose) inside the round&#x27;s endorsement
   window, the optional lender-bridge filter, then 1:1 or margin tiers; write one
   crosswalk tagged with match_round

`--era pre2018 --step bridge` builds only the FHA-mortgagee ↔
HMDA-respondent bridge that step 3 reads. It reads FHA silver, the HMDA panel and
the HMDA loan register -- never a crosswalk -- so the yield it unlocks is not
circular. Both sources are closed, so it rebuilds on a method change or an
upstream silver rebuild (with --overwrite), not on the annual HMDA cycle.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match hmda-fha run
  mortgage-data match hmda-fha run --era pre2018 --step bridge
  mortgage-data match hmda-fha run --era pre2018

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-fha run [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--era <str>`: Matching era: &#x27;post2018&#x27; (default) or &#x27;pre2018&#x27; (2010-2017)  [default: post2018]
* `--step <str>`: match (default), or bridge: pre2018 only, build just the lender bridge the pre-2018 match reads  [default: match]
* `-m, --min-year <int>`: Minimum year to match (default: the era&#x27;s)
* `-M, --max-year <int>`: Maximum year to match (default: the era&#x27;s)
* `--overwrite`: Rebuild the data-prep intermediates even if they exist
* `--fha-dir <path>`: Override FHA silver data directory
* `--hmda-dir <path>`: Override HMDA silver data directory
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Override output directory
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-fha build-zip-tract`

Build consolidated ZIP-tract crosswalk from HUD data.

The HUD crosswalk uses different census tract vintages:
- 2010: Census tracts used for years 2010-2019
- 2020: Census tracts used for years 2020+

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-fha build-zip-tract [OPTIONS] {census_vintage}
```

**Arguments**:

* `census_vintage`: Census vintage (2010 or 2020)  [required]

**Options**:

* `-o, --output <path>`: Output path for crosswalk file
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-fha validate`

Run validation analysis and generate diagnostic figures.

Checks the HMDA-FHA crosswalk&#x27;s match quality by year, geography and
loan characteristics.

Each era writes one combined figure plus the state and county choropleths
(plotly, so they cannot share the grid) into its own figure directory.

--era post2018 (default) panels: match rates over time, by loan amount, by
interest rate, by loan purpose, by rate type, by HMDA submission channel,
and the state and county size-vs-match-rate scatters.

--era pre2018 panels: match rates by year, round contribution, the
lender-bridge placebo controls, loan amount, loan purpose, and the same
size-vs-match-rate scatters. It also prints the era&#x27;s own evidence -
agreement with the frozen 2010-2017 reference artifact, the held-out
round-1 lender-agreement test, and the selection-bias tables. There is no
interest-rate panel; pre-2018 HMDA carries no interest rate.

Era-invalid flags are rejected rather than ignored.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-fha validate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--era <str>`: Matching era: &#x27;post2018&#x27; (default) or &#x27;pre2018&#x27; (2010-2017)  [default: post2018]
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Directory to save validation figures
* `--save-plots / --no-save-plots`: Save plots to disk  [default: save-plots]
* `--show-plots`: Display plots interactively
* `--min-loans <int>`: Minimum loans for county filtering  [default: 50]
* `--skip-placebo`: pre2018 only: skip the bridge placebo controls
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-fhfa run`

--era post2018 (default) runs the rounds in `ROUNDS_POST2018` (rounds.py; see `info`). It

### `mortgage-data match hmda-gse`

HMDA-GSE matching workflow: HMDA conventional loans ↔ GSE loan-level records, by the chain (HMDA → FHFA → MBS → UMBS) and by a direct match

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gse [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `info`: Show information about HMDA-GSE matching...
* `run`: Build the HMDA-GSE crosswalks.
* `lender-crosswalk`: Build lender/seller crosswalk for name...
* `validate`: Run validation analysis on HMDA-GSE matches.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-gse info`

Show information about HMDA-GSE matching configuration and data availability.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gse info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-gse run`

Build the HMDA-GSE crosswalks.

The chain composes the upstream crosswalks per enterprise: HMDA-FHFA, then FHFA-MBS
(extended matching), then MBS-UMBS; --enrich adds HMDA loan fields and UMBS seller
info. Output: crosswalk/hmda_gse/hmda_gse_crosswalk_chain_{agency}.parquet.

The direct match links HMDA straight to the combined loan-issuance spine (no FHFA
leg). It first builds the lender bridge (lender names from HMDA&#x27;s own filings, plus
names learned from a characteristics-only pass) and saves it, or with --saved-bridge
reads the saved one. Then the rounds in rounds.py run in order, each on the loans
earlier rounds left: a name-pinned round and a nameless one, blocking on ZIP3, $10k
amount bin, 3-decimal rate, term, coarse purpose and occupancy, with a quarter-aware
origination window. The rounds always run over the whole year window; the year
options choose which files are written. Every row carries its ``disposition``
against the chain and an ``fhfa_verdict``. Output:
crosswalk/hmda_gse/hmda_gse_crosswalk_direct_{year}.parquet and
hmda_gse_lender_bridge.parquet.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match hmda-gse run
  mortgage-data match hmda-gse run --route chain --agency fnma --enrich
  mortgage-data match hmda-gse run --route direct --min-year 2024 --overwrite
  mortgage-data match hmda-gse run --route direct --saved-bridge --overwrite

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gse run [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-r, --route <str>`: chain (HMDA → FHFA → MBS → UMBS), direct (HMDA ↔ combined loan issuance), or all (chain first: the direct match reads it)  [default: all]
* `-a, --agency <str>`: Chain only: fnma, fhlmc, or all  [default: all]
* `-m, --min-year <int>`: Minimum HMDA activity year  [default: 2018]
* `-M, --max-year <int>`: Maximum HMDA activity year  [default: 2025]
* `-e, --enrich`: Chain only: also write the enriched crosswalk
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Chain only: write the crosswalks here
* `--overwrite`: Direct only: rebuild years that already exist and rerun the bridge pass
* `--keep-double-claims`: Direct only: admit increment rows whose target the chain already claims (not recommended)
* `--saved-bridge`: Direct only: block on the saved lender bridge instead of rebuilding it
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-gse lender-crosswalk`

Build lender/seller crosswalk for name mismatches.

Identifies HMDA lenders and UMBS sellers that frequently match but have
different names. These represent mergers, acquisitions, rebrands, affiliates,
and DBAs worth documenting.

The analysis focuses on Retail channel by default, where the originating
lender is expected to be the same as the seller to the GSEs.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gse lender-crosswalk [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-l, --min-loans <int>`: Minimum number of matched loans to include a pair  [default: 100]
* `-c, --channel <str>`: Channel to filter on (R=Retail, C=Correspondent, B=Broker)  [default: R]
* `-r, --report`: Generate markdown documentation report
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Override output directory
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-gse validate`

Run validation analysis on HMDA-GSE matches.

Writes one combined figure, hmda_gse_validation.png, covering both directions
across the combined crosswalks (chain + direct match): the HMDA-to-UMBS match
rate by activity year, and the UMBS-to-HMDA match rate by first payment date.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match hmda-gse validate --show-plots
  mortgage-data match hmda-gse validate --min-year 2020 --max-year 2023
  mortgage-data match hmda-gse validate --direct

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gse validate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--min-year <int>`: Minimum activity year  [default: 2018]
* `--max-year <int>`: Maximum activity year  [default: 2025]
* `-s, --show-plots`: Show the figure interactively
* `--save / --no-save`: Save the figure to docs/matching/figures/  [default: save]
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Override output directory for the figure
* `--direct`: Instead score the direct crosswalk on held-out fields (borrowers, destination, chain concordance), by disposition and FHFA verdict
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data match hmda-gnma`

HMDA-GNMA matching workflow (HMDA FHA and VA/USDA loans ↔ GNMA loan-level)

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gnma [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `info`: Show the HMDA-GNMA configuration and which...
* `run`: Match HMDA government originations to GNMA...
* `validate`: Score HMDA-GNMA crosswalks by aggregator ↔...

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-gnma info`

Show the HMDA-GNMA configuration and which crosswalks exist.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gnma info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-gnma run`

Match HMDA government originations to GNMA loan-level disclosures.

FHA: an FHA-enriched direct match. Each FHA-matched HMDA loan carries its FHA record&#x27;s
exact amount and endorsement month (through the hmda_fha crosswalk) plus HMDA&#x27;s exact
rate and term, and is scored on units, borrowers, MIP-aware CLTV, month, LEI-issuer
dyads and DTI. Pairs enter on the score floor, or on absent CLTV/DTI evidence when
everything present agrees.

VA/USDA (HMDA loan_type 3/4 -&gt; GNMA Agency V/R): a pure scored direct match with no
administrative bridge -- exact-rate/term/year blocking in $10k amount bins, fee-aware
CLTV, one-sided DTI, purpose evidence, LEI-issuer dyads, and purchaser-type-aware
retail identity alignment, then a third round over the cells the cell cap dropped,
sub-blocked on purpose x units x borrowers.

Output: crosswalk/hmda_gnma/hmda_gnma_crosswalk_{fha,va_usda}.parquet.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match hmda-gnma run
  mortgage-data match hmda-gnma run --loan-type fha --min-score 14
  mortgage-data match hmda-gnma run --loan-type va-usda --capped-min-score 11

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gnma run [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --loan-type <str>`: Population to match: fha, va-usda, or all  [default: all]
* `-m, --min-year <int>`: Minimum HMDA activity year  [default: 2018]
* `-M, --max-year <int>`: Maximum HMDA activity year  [default: 2025]
* `--min-score <int>`: total_score floor (default: FHA 11, &gt;=14 strict; VA/USDA 9 for rounds 1-2, where score=12 is a medium-confidence pocket)
* `--capped-min-score <int>`: VA/USDA only: total_score floor for round 3, the capped-cell round (5 of it is its own key)
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: FHA only: write the crosswalk here instead of crosswalk/
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match hmda-gnma validate`

Score HMDA-GNMA crosswalks by aggregator ↔ issuer name triangulation.

`aggregator` is the share of testable pairs whose purchaser (aggregator) panel
name matches the pool issuer name; `originator_ctrl` is the same test against
the originator and should stay low. The gauge uses no field the matchers key on.
The sellers/purchasers -&gt; LEI pair table it scores against is built on first use.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match hmda-gnma validate
  mortgage-data match hmda-gnma validate --loan-type fha --by source
  mortgage-data match hmda-gnma validate --crosswalk staged.parquet --by match_round

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match hmda-gnma validate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --loan-type <str>`: Crosswalk to score: fha, va-usda, or all  [default: all]
* `--crosswalk <path>`: Score this parquet instead (needs HMDAIndex and issuer_id or gnma_loan_id)
* `--by <str>`: Also score per value of this column
* `-m, --min-year <int>`: First HMDA year  [default: 2018]
* `-M, --max-year <int>`: Last HMDA year (default: all)
* `--overwrite`: Rebuild the sellers/purchasers -&gt; LEI pair table (after an s/p or HMDA rebuild)
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data match mbs-umbs`

MBS-UMBS matching workflow commands (MBS ↔ UMBS)

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match mbs-umbs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `run`: Match GSE single-family loans (the MBS...
* `info`: Display MBS matching configuration and...
* `check`: Check the latest matcher run against...
* `validate`: Run validation analysis on MBS-UMBS...

#### `mortgage-data match mbs-umbs run`

Match GSE single-family loans (the MBS side) to UMBS disclosures.

Both sides are two releases by default. The MBS side adds Fannie&#x27;s separately
published HARP/Refi Plus population (silver/harp) to the quarterly files; the UMBS side
adds the first monthly snapshot (MLLD/FU) to post-2019 ILLD, recovering loans
originated before ILLD coverage began (2019-06).

Output: crosswalk/mbs_umbs/mbs_umbs_crosswalk_{agency}.parquet, with a metrics sidecar.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs run
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs run --agency fnma
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs run --agency fnma --no-harp
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs run --no-snapshot --no-exact-attribute-round

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match mbs-umbs run [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-a, --agency <str>`: GSE to match: fnma, fhlmc, or all  [default: all]
* `--snapshot / --no-snapshot`: Recover pre-2019 loans from the first monthly snapshot (MLLD/FU). --no-snapshot reverts to the post-2019 ILLD-only matcher.  [default: snapshot]
* `--harp / --no-harp`: Include Fannie&#x27;s separately-released HARP/Refi Plus population in the MBS universe (FNMA only; Freddie has no equivalent release).  [default: harp]
* `--null-tolerant / --no-null-tolerant`: Let a tolerance check pass when either side&#x27;s value is missing, so one absent attribute cannot veto an otherwise-agreeing candidate. --no-null-tolerant is the null-vetoing baseline.  [default: null-tolerant]
* `--exact-attribute-round / --no-exact-attribute-round`: Run round 4, which resolves leftover candidate groups on exactness over LTV/CLTV/DTI/Term and drops every tie. --no-exact-attribute-round reverts to the three-round matcher.  [default: exact-attribute-round]
* `-v, --verbose`: Show detailed progress output
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match mbs-umbs check`

Check the latest matcher run against pinned match-rate floors (drift guard).

Every matcher run writes a metrics sidecar (mbs_umbs_crosswalk_{agency}_metrics.json)
next to the crosswalk. This command compares it against the floors pinned in
expected_match_rates.json and exits non-zero on any breach — run it after regenerating
a crosswalk, especially following upstream import-layer rebuilds (fnma/fhlmc/umbs).

It also re-counts the matcher&#x27;s input globs and reports any crosswalk whose inputs have
changed size since it was built. That is a warning, not a breach: the crosswalk is not
wrong, it is behind. Mtimes do not catch it — an input directory can grow while every
file in it stays older than the crosswalk.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs check
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs check --agency fnma

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match mbs-umbs check [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-a, --agency <str>`: GSE to check: fnma, fhlmc, or all  [default: all]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match mbs-umbs validate`

Run validation analysis on MBS-UMBS matches (both GSEs).

combined diagnostic figure (mbs_umbs_match_rates_panel.png): match rates by month,
interest rate, FICO, LTV, and DTI, with loan distributions and underwriting cut
points on each characteristic panel.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs validate
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs validate --show-plots
  mortgage-data match mbs-umbs validate --no-save

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match mbs-umbs validate [OPTIONS]
```

* `--save / --no-save`: Save the figure to docs/matching/figures/  [default: save]

#### `mortgage-data match crt-mbs run`

Link GSE CRT reference-pool loans to the SF loan-level datasets.

FHLMC: per deal, the rounds in rounds.py (exact joins, 1:1 both directions) against the SF
origination silver, then UPB-at-issuance confirmation against the performance panel
(cent-exact within ±1 month of the deal Period). Output:
`crosswalk/crt_mbs/crt_mbs_crosswalk_fhlmc.parquet` plus a per-deal summary.

FNMA: extracts CAS/CIRT deal membership, streaming the `CAS_*.zip` /
`CIRT_*.zip` historical downloads in fnma raw when present (one ~350 GB
decompressing pass, ~30 min), else scanning the SF performance bronze. The extracted
ids are the CRT-specific `CRT Loan Identifier` and do NOT join to the LPPUB
Loan Identifier. Output: `crosswalk/crt_mbs/crt_mbs_crosswalk_fnma.parquet`.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match crt-mbs run --agency fhlmc
  mortgage-data match crt-mbs run --agency fhlmc -d 19DNA1 -d 24DNA3 --no-confirm
  mortgage-data match crt-mbs run --agency fnma

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match crt-mbs run [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-a, --agency <str>`: GSE to link: fhlmc, fnma, or all  [default: all]
* `-d, --deals <str>`: FHLMC only: match just these Reference Pool Numbers (default: every deal in silver/crt)
* `--confirm / --no-confirm`: FHLMC only: confirm pins against the SF performance panel (UPB at issuance, ±1 month)  [default: confirm]
* `-v, --verbose`: Show detailed progress
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data match master`

Master crosswalk: the HMDA spine assembled from every matching workflow

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match master [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `build`: Assemble the spine, QC it, and promote it...
* `qc`: Run the invariant suite and print the result.
* `info`: Report what is on disk: inputs,...

#### `mortgage-data match master build`

Assemble the spine, QC it, and promote it to `crosswalk/master/`.

The build lands in a private staging tree first so a QC failure can never
replace a good artifact; promotion is partition-scoped, so a single-year
rebuild only ever touches that year.

Staging QC sees only the years just built, so the POOLED invariants (target
exclusivity across every year) are re-checked against the whole artifact
after promotion. That second pass is what would catch a partial rebuild
leaving the artifact internally inconsistent.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match master build
  mortgage-data match master build --min-year 2024 --overwrite
  mortgage-data match master build --no-promote      # stage + QC only

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match master build [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--min-year <int>`: First activity year (default 2018)
* `--max-year <int>`: Last activity year (default 2025)
* `--overwrite`: Rebuild years already staged
* `--promote / --no-promote`: Promote to crosswalk/master/ when QC passes  [default: promote]
* `--verify / --no-verify`: Re-run QC over the whole promoted artifact (catches pooled violations)  [default: verify]
* `-v, --verbose`: Show detailed progress
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `mortgage-data match master qc`

Run the invariant suite and print the result.

Checks grain (one row per HMDA loan), pooled target exclusivity, the
agency/enterprise cross-matcher agreement, and the reconciliation of
``mbs_without_fhfa`` against the ``direct_no_link`` count.

Examples:
  mortgage-data match master qc --crosswalk

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match master qc [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--crosswalk`: Audit the promoted crosswalk instead of staging
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Report what is on disk: inputs, partitions, coverage, last QC.

Examples:

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data match master info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `mortgage-data usps-crosswalk`

USPS ZIP crosswalk data operations

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data usps-crosswalk [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `-V, --version`: Show version and exit
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `download`: Download USPS crosswalk data from the HUD...
* `bronze`: Build per-quarter bronze parquet from raw...
* `pipeline`: Bring the crosswalks up to date: download...
* `validate`: Check bronze coverage and ratio sums.
* `info`: Display USPS crosswalk configuration and...

### `mortgage-data usps-crosswalk download`

Download USPS crosswalk data from the HUD API.

Downloads all 12 crosswalk types from the HUD USPS API. Requires
USPS_CROSSWALK_API_KEY to be set in your .env file or environment.

**Note:** The API &#x27;query=All&#x27; parameter only works
reliably for 2021+ data. Pre-2021 data may return errors.

**Examples:**

  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk download
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk download -t ZIP_TRACT -t TRACT_ZIP
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk download --min-year 2021 --pause 2 --verbose

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data usps-crosswalk download [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Crosswalk types to process (default: all 12)
* `--min-year <int>`: First year (default: each type&#x27;s own start)
* `--max-year <int>`: Last year (default: through the current quarter)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `--pause SECONDS`: Seconds to pause between downloads. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data usps-crosswalk bronze`

Build per-quarter bronze parquet from raw JSON.

Reads each quarter&#x27;s untouched raw JSON, enforces the schema (zero-padded
geographic codes, numeric ratios), and writes a per-quarter parquet. Bronze
is the analysis layer for this source — read across quarters with
``load_crosswalk()`` / ``load_crosswalk_by_vintage()`` rather than building
a combined file.

**Examples:**

  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk bronze
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk bronze --datasets ZIP_TRACT --datasets TRACT_ZIP
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk bronze --min-year 2015 --max-year 2024

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data usps-crosswalk bronze [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Crosswalk types to process (default: all 12)
* `--min-year <int>`: First year (default: each type&#x27;s own start)
* `--max-year <int>`: Last year (default: through the current quarter)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data usps-crosswalk pipeline`

Bring the crosswalks up to date: download → bronze.

The normal way to run this source. Both steps skip what is already on disk,
so a bare pipeline asks HUD for anything newer than what you
have, fetches it, and builds the parquet. Safe to re-run any time.

**Examples:**

  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk pipeline
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk pipeline -t ZIP_TRACT -t TRACT_ZIP
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk pipeline --skip-download

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data usps-crosswalk pipeline [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Crosswalk types to process (default: all 12)
* `--min-year <int>`: First year (default: each type&#x27;s own start)
* `--max-year <int>`: Last year (default: through the current quarter)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `--pause SECONDS`: Seconds to pause between downloads. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `--skip-download`: Build bronze from the raw already present
* `--skip-bronze`: Fetch raw only
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data usps-crosswalk validate`

Check bronze coverage and ratio sums.

Reports quarters HUD should have published that are missing from bronze,
and source geographies whose allocation ratios don&#x27;t sum to ~1.0.

**Examples:**

  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk validate
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk validate ZIP_TRACT
  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk validate all --skip-ratios

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data usps-crosswalk validate [OPTIONS] [crosswalk_type]
```

**Arguments**:

* `crosswalk_type`: Crosswalk type to validate, or &#x27;all&#x27;  [default: all]

**Options**:

* `--skip-ratios`: Skip the per-quarter ratio-sum check
* `--sample-quarters <int>`: Quarters to ratio-check per type  [default: 4]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data usps-crosswalk info`

Display USPS crosswalk configuration and crosswalk type information.

**Examples:**

  mortgage-data usps-crosswalk info

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data usps-crosswalk info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhlb download`

Download raw FHLB artifacts.

Datasets (default all):
  - `ama`: Acquired Member Assets loan-level CSVs
  - `members`: quarterly member-institution Excel files

Each dataset lands in its own configured directory; `--output-dir`
overrides that and so requires exactly one dataset.

**Examples:**

  mortgage-data fhlb download
  mortgage-data fhlb download -t ama -o /custom/path


* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets to download: ama, members, dictionaries (repeatable; default all)
* `-o, --output-dir <path>`: Output directory (single dataset only)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `--pause SECONDS`: Seconds to pause between downloads. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `--timeout SECONDS`: Request timeout in seconds. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `--retries COUNT`: Number of retry attempts for failed downloads. Default: 3
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhlb bronze`

Import raw FHLB artifacts to the bronze layer.

Datasets (default all):
  - `ama`: AMA CSVs -&gt; parquet with standardized column names
  - `members`: member Excel files -&gt; one parquet per quarter

AMA and members have different published year ranges, so omitting
`--min-year`/`--max-year` resolves each independently.

**Examples:**

  $ mortgage-data fhlb bronze
  $ mortgage-data fhlb bronze -t ama --min-year 2020 --max-year 2024
  $ mortgage-data fhlb bronze --overwrite

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhlb bronze [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets to import: ama, members (repeatable; default all)
* `--min-year <int>`: Earliest year (default: per-dataset)
* `--max-year <int>`: Latest year (default: per-dataset)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhlb silver`

Transform FHLB bronze data to the silver layer.

Applies data quality transformations including:
- Normalizing percentage values across schema versions
- Fixing income amount units
- Standardizing indicator variable encoding
- Cleaning census tract identifiers
- Replacing sentinel missing values with nulls

**Examples:**

  $ mortgage-data fhlb silver
  $ mortgage-data fhlb silver --min-year 2020 --max-year 2024
  $ mortgage-data fhlb silver --overwrite

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhlb silver [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-t, --datasets <str>`: Datasets to transform: ama (repeatable; default all)
* `--min-year <int>`: Earliest year (default: per-dataset)
* `--max-year <int>`: Latest year (default: per-dataset)
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhlb pipeline`

Run the complete FHLB AMA pipeline (download -&gt; bronze -&gt; silver).

AMA is FHLB&#x27;s end-to-end flow; members data has no silver stage, so build it
with `fhlb bronze -t members`.

**Examples:**

  $ mortgage-data fhlb pipeline
  $ mortgage-data fhlb pipeline --min-year 2020 --max-year 2024
  $ mortgage-data fhlb pipeline --skip-download
  $ mortgage-data fhlb pipeline --skip-download --skip-silver

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhlb pipeline [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--min-year <int>`: Earliest year (default: per-dataset)
* `--max-year <int>`: Latest year (default: per-dataset)
* `--skip-download`: Skip download step (use existing raw files)
* `--skip-bronze`: Skip bronze loading step
* `--skip-silver`: Skip silver transformation step
* `--overwrite`: Overwrite existing files instead of skipping them.
* `--pause SECONDS`: Seconds to pause between downloads. Default: the source&#x27;s configured value.
* `-v, --verbose`: Enable verbose (DEBUG level) logging output.
* `-q, --quiet`: Suppress progress bars and reduce output.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data fhlb info`

Display FHLB configuration information.

Shows the current configuration paths and settings for FHLB data.

  fhlb info

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data fhlb info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `mortgage-data raw`

Raw download ledger: register, audit, changes, info

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data raw [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `register`: Record every raw file that has no ledger...
* `audit`: List raw files with no...
* `changes`: Destinations acquired more than once with...
* `info`: Ledger location and, per source, files on...

### `mortgage-data raw register`

Record every raw file that has no ledger record yet (hashes each file).

Resumable: files whose latest record already matches their size are skipped.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data raw register [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-s, --source <str>`: Source(s) to act on. Default: all known sources.
* `--method <str>`: &#x27;manual&#x27; for hand-placed files; &#x27;backfill&#x27; for the one-time baseline of a raw layer that predates the ledger.  [default: manual]
* `--note <str>`: Provenance note stored on every record.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data raw audit`

List raw files with no successful/registered ledger record (or a size mismatch).

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data raw audit [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-s, --source <str>`: Source(s) to act on. Default: all known sources.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data raw changes`

Destinations acquired more than once with different bytes (upstream revisions).

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data raw changes [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-s, --source <str>`: Source(s) to act on. Default: all known sources.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `mortgage-data raw info`

Ledger location and, per source, files on record and the last run.

**Usage**:

```console
$ mortgage-data raw info [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-s, --source <str>`: Source(s) to act on. Default: all known sources.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.
